newsitem.title: USA: CS First Boston says sees no basis for SEC action.
newsitem.headline: CS First Boston says sees no basis for SEC action.

text.p: CS First Boston Corp said Wednesday there was no basis for the Securities and Exchange Commission's civil action against the firm for alleged fraud in the offer and sale of Orange County, Calif., bonds.
"We believe that there is no basis for a fraud charge and we will defend the action vigorously," a spokesman for the firm said in a statement. CS First Boston is an affiliate of CS Holding.
In its complaint, the SEC alleged fraud in the offer and sale of $110 million of Series B pension obligation bonds issued by Orange County in September 1994.

While preparing the bond offering documents, the SEC alleged that CS First Boston officials "knew, or were reckless in not knowing, significant negative information about the county (investment) pools that was misrepresented in or omitted from the official (bond) statement."
CS First Boston said the SEC action was a "technical dispute" over how much investigation and disclosure is required by an underwriter in a municipal bond offering.

"The county provided CS First Boston with misleading information about the (county investment) pool, and CS First Boston was clearly victimized by (former Orange County Treasurer) Robert Citron's information about the pool," the CS First Boston spokesman said.
He added that CS First Boston has cooperated fully with the SEC throughout its investigation. Sources said the firm was not currently in settlement talks with the SEC.
CS First Boston said the SEC action does not implicate the firm in any other aspect of the Orange County financial crisis, which the firm charged was generated by Citron.
"CS First Boston was not an advisor to Mr. Citron, and Mr. Citron refused to give CS First Boston detailed information regarding the investment pool's portfolio," the firm said.

"The firm had no knowledge, other than what was publicly known, about Citron's investment strategies or the related criminal activities to which he has since pleaded guilty," the firm said in the statement.

CS First Boston said the pension bond offering was the only Orange County bond offering in which CS First Boston acted as lead underwriter. CS First Boston added that the county repaid its Series B bonds in full.
CS First Boston left the municipal finance business in February 1995 and no longer underwriters municipal bonds.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
